title: Readable worked land
changes: Mines, mills and pastures now gain close detail at the same camera scale as their towns, keeping the wider landscape easier to read.
Stable site-based mirrored layouts vary the countryside without moving paid sites or changing their operation; far pasture shelters retain visible supports.
Exact installed inventory, construction, inspection and simulation remain unchanged.

title: Skylines earned by each town
changes: Installed local industrial and launch infrastructure now gives homes a distinct, compact masonry or stepped silhouette while retaining each civilization’s material and roof identity.
Small seeded height differences stay attached to the same town lots across growth, camera detail and reload. Primitive and civic homes, exact inventory and unfinished construction remain unchanged.
This is an observational visual update: no new facilities, production, residents or simulation rules are created.

title: Food, households and resilient supply
changes: A distinct local Food world ties harvests to actual geography, wellbeing, damage and staffed facilities instead of infrastructure amplification, with 1.25 Food per Earth resident each strategic season.

Town inspection separates recorded production, required meals, actual household spending and growth payment against shared civilization reserves. Autonomous forecasts and new relief terms use the same versioned rule.

Prior living worlds keep their original names, rules, controller memories and read-only histories. Hosted policy changes are refused until an explicit compatible rollout; Mars cargo and colony upkeep are unchanged.
Conditional relief remains conserved and voluntary. Natural resilience, cooperation and earned Mars outcomes require separate observation, not guaranteed aid or artificial famine.

title: Names shaped by each civilization
changes: Fresh generated worlds use seeded culture-shaped town names grounded in their real founding locality, with bounded collision handling rather than numbered settlement labels.
Names are recorded once at capital creation or successful founding. Older worlds, their recorded names and histories remain untouched; this update does not reset an existing living world.
Town names do not change simulation randomness, settlement identity, resource costs, controller choices or legal action IDs.

title: Relief, local consequences and a new living world
changes: Civilizations can offer one-way Food relief over an existing consenting corridor, accept or withdraw exact terms, and pay a conserved later transfer from real supplies. Promises are not stocks and shortages cause no invented penalty.

Regional events choose a seeded eligible town and exact local attachment, retain that selection through commands and replay, and record immediate costs and before/after consequences without silently choosing another target.

The latest Living world gets one new locked, persisted genesis and seed. Living partnerships, previous generated worlds and the first local world remain untouched, separately selectable read-only histories.
This is a new local-observatory release, not an upgrade of old saves or activation of the shared hosted world. Broader campaigns, platform behavior and visual delivery remain separately evidenced.

title: A more readable working landscape
changes: Mine and Lumber mill sites use compact, lower silhouettes at middle and distant zoom while close details, construction states and the complete inspection inventory remain available.
Chronicle cards name recorded causes and consequences in plain language; the original technical event text remains available in Events.
Existing worlds, simulation rules and autonomous decisions are unchanged. Wider visual and device acceptance remains ongoing.

title: Living partnerships and local history
changes: Civilizations weigh useful paid trade, negotiated repairs, urgent recovery and alternative suppliers against current needs and available supplies; promises, completed work and delivered cargo remain distinct.
Six qualified regional events bring invested harvests, forest fires, coastal storms, trade fairs, industrial accidents and conserved internal migration with recorded local causes and consequences.
Compact specialized town compositions and original faction crests keep installed landmarks legible without repeating every building at the same oversized scale.
Chronicle cards expose recorded causes and results; inspection makes all active construction towns reachable without issuing faction commands.
The new content world is a separate genesis. Previous generated and first local worlds remain untouched, selectable read-only histories; general varied-world succession remains future work.

title: Two worlds, one recorded history
changes: Earth towns distinguish hearth settlements, civic fabric, installed industry and launch infrastructure from local built assets rather than the shared world stage. Unfinished paid work stays visibly unfinished; active cues require actual current operations.

An observational Earth/Mars switch brings recorded colony habitats, inhabitants, delivered reserve cargo and in-flight missions into the main viewport. Red terrain is illustrative context, not new simulated territory, resources or local production.
Earth and Mars retain separate source- and genesis-qualified cameras and selections. Journey history remains available, and a completed world never advances because another body is inspected.

Versioned bounded history readers expose exact recorded construction and operation details with strict revision fences and private-field exclusions. Existing public archive reads retain their original format.
Rendering models, interaction tests and typed history evidence remain separate from browser art acceptance, WebGL/touch performance and managed-host validation.

title: From first hearths to a supplied Mars home
changes: New generated worlds have coherent terrain, separated inland and coastal starts, viable paid expansion and finite Iron and Coal. Earlier local and native worlds retain their original maps, resources and history.

Weighted civilization policies connect coastal settlement, staffed production, funded research and genuinely faster consensual steam trade to planetary knowledge. Decisions still pay the canonical costs; no language-model players or player orders are introduced.

A powered launch complex sends prepaid cargo and conserved settlers on a delayed journey. Landed supplies fund habitat construction and colony upkeep separately from Earth reserves. Only an inhabited, completed habitat supplied for consecutive seasons establishes a Mars home; shortage and paid recovery remain real consequences.

Retained earned milestones support explicit historical date advances without replacing the ordinary clock or unlocking mechanics through the calendar. The journey view distinguishes preparation, transport, landing, paid habitat work and stable life; its colony schematic is not a geographical surface map.

The generated observatory is separate from the read-only previous local world and shared archive. World-qualified camera preferences avoid cross-world jumps. If coordinated storage is unavailable, an explicitly labelled this-tab simulation continues without writing shared checkpoints.

A bounded default-seed campaign follows the exact local engine used by the Worker from empty settlements to sustained Mars life, including exact restart and a separately fault-injected recovery. Wider-seed balance, richer city-age visuals, supported-browser evidence and genuinely unattended hosting remain distinct acceptance work.

title: A world that makes its own decisions
changes: Five distinct seeded civilization policies and a procedural World Director choose real research, civic commitments, construction, expansion, repair and exchange. They use the same rules and resource costs as the preserved historical world, without runtime language-model calls.

The default observatory is a separate accelerated local world that runs while this browser is open. Versioned checkpoints preserve progress and policy state; background simulation keeps camera and inspection separate from decision work. Shared history remains a distinct read-only view.

A map-first navy-and-brass interface brings civilization identity, current pursuits, connected civic progress and meaningful recent events together. Terrain relief, coasts, town silhouettes and map detail follow actual world facts. Humans only observe.

Protected shared-host activation and bounded simulation wakes now retain exact policy provenance and durable receipts. No unattended scheduler is claimed or silently enabled, and the existing native world and historical model-agent records are not reset.

This is the first zero-player milestone. A stronger new-world geography generator and the remaining earned Stone Age-to-Mars progression are ongoing work, not capabilities unlocked by this viewer release.

title: Inhabited towns and powered research
changes: Chiefdom and Autocracy offer different Food, original-capital construction and policy-slot choices. Inspection keeps the active government, pending transition, commitment and current work capacity separate from historical construction.

The map uses population-based residential density, broader completed Farm fields and Workshop yards, plus clearer ownership washes and borders. Terrain and exact sites remain factual; symbolic houses do not represent individual residents, and unfinished buildings are not drawn as completed.

Sanitation and Chemistry connect productive research to an era-three Research laboratory at the same town’s completed Campus. A Laboratory costs 42 Materials, 24 Credits and 18 construction work before it can operate.

A staffed Laboratory reserves two opening Credits, three local Power and three residents together for twelve base Science under existing output modifiers. Inspection shows actual Science, payments and allocations separately from base output. The town’s bounded last-positive record can be replaced by a later productive beat.

This source prepares a separate compatible activation. Actual agent government choices and Laboratory operation need their own live evidence. Matched public map views, narrow-screen use and physical-device checks remain open.

title: A government choice for the capital
changes: Five connected civics lead from Code of laws to Political philosophy through Culture produced in later seasons. Agents can then explicitly choose Autocracy and its exact policy slots.
Chiefdom adds one base Food in every owned town. Autocracy adds 15% construction work only in the original capital while it remains owned, with two military, one economic and one wildcard slot.

A government change keeps the active arrangement for two working beats at 75% ordinary output before the target begins its four-beat commitment. Inspection separates active and pending arrangements, exact slots, current town capacity and recorded order work.

This source prepares a separate compatible activation. Actual agent adoption and later capital work need their own live evidence. Historical construction receives no retroactive bonus; public narrow-screen and physical-device checks remain open.

title: Coal powers a town Factory
changes: The compatible local Power release follows the industrial chain. Agents can pay for a Coal plant and Factory in a town with the required Industrial zone and industrial capability. Construction and later operation remain separate.

A staffed plant pays two opening Coal to generate eight Power for its town and season. A staffed Factory consumes three Power for twelve base Materials under the existing output modifiers. Unused Power expires; stored Energy and later supplies cannot replace opening fuel.

Town and capability inspection show the actual Coal payment, local residents, generated and consumed Power, expiry, Materials and receipt-only emissions. The latest attempt stays separate from the last positive Factory result, including after a pause or history pruning.

This source update does not activate the compatible releases by itself. Actual inhabited-world operation, public device evidence, advanced project-work bonuses and unattended calendar scheduling remain separate outcomes.

title: Coal powers faster trade
changes: Scientific method, Shipbuilding, Industrialization and Steam power connect existing research to finite Coal. An enabled Mine uses its existing local residents to extract Coal into a separate, capacity-limited stock.

Agents can pay for exact owned Rail edges in a named town’s construction lane. A new steam agreement needs fresh consent and keeps its original path, speed and fuel cost; earlier agreements do not change.

A successful due steam exchange pays all cargo, upkeep and one proposer Coal together. Town Work and route inspection show paid Rail, actual fuel use and recorded cadence beside the original unrailed comparison.

The industrial capability requires two towns that actually operated supplied Foundries and one genuinely faster paid steam delivery. Civic and industrial activation remain separate from publishing this compatible source. Local Power, Factories and unattended calendar scheduling remain outside this packet.

title: Culture becomes a civic choice
changes: The compatible civic release adds a separate Culture lane. Agents can choose Code of laws and complete it using Culture actually produced in later seasons; stored Culture does not skip the commitment.

Chiefdom and Urban planning require an explicit agent choice. The government adds base Food and the policy adds base construction work at later openings. The exact reform entitlement, payment and commitment stay in the world record.
Town inspection separates current government slots and base contributions from recorded construction work and past output. The spectator cannot adopt a government or change a policy.
Publication prepares a separate compatible civic activation. Automatic unattended calendar scheduling, advanced governments, Coal, steam and powered factories are not delivered by this packet.

title: Town production at a glance
changes: Town Overview shows the latest recorded output from completed paid-input buildings, including Foundries, Observatories and Printing houses. Inputs and local residents come from actual operation receipts.
Current On or Paused settings stay separate from the last recorded round and output. Missing records and blocked production are stated without inventing results.
Choose a production row to open its exact Work details. The three newest installed paid buildings stay visible; a compact disclosure retains the rest.
This presentation update preserves the existing world, resource economy and calendar. Civic and industrial successors remain separate work.

title: Learning follows the land
changes: Sailing, Celestial navigation and Astronomy connect research to a same-town Observatory. Eligibility comes from actual high ground beside the completed Campus, with its exact qualifying source retained.

A timber Observatory foundation becomes a rounded tower beside the existing Library and University. Work distinguishes paid construction, completion and later Credits plus local residents producing recorded Science.

Current high-ground options remain separate from the historical Campus and source. Local desktop and360/400 CSS-width views expose Made and Used together; tiny overview recognition, shallow mobile map space and public-origin browser observation remain open.
Publication prepares a separate compatible Observatory activation. Coal, steam, powered factories and climate effects are not delivered by this packet.

title: Iron becomes useful industrial work
changes: Military engineering, Gunpowder and Metal casting connect existing research to a same-town Industrial-zone Foundry. Its operating recipe consumes recorded Iron and Energy with local residents to produce Materials.
A real supplied Foundry can create strategic storage room for a later full consensual iron shipment. Completion itself produces nothing, and shortages or pauses spend neither resource ledger.

Focused Work and recipe details show Iron separately from ordinary Energy and Materials. A completed furnace annex differs from its construction foundation; current pause remains separate from the last recorded operation.

Local desktop and360/400 CSS-width views are checked. Tiny overview recognition, direct site activation and public-origin browser verification remain open. Observatory and later industrial power content are not active in this packet.

title: Culture grows in inhabited places
changes: Construction and Printing connect useful research to exact Theater sites and same-town Printing houses. Completed wonders add a recorded nearby Culture bonus; unfinished contenders do not.
Theater foundations become an open court and stage. Printing construction becomes an annex, while focused Work separates completion from later paid Materials and resident-supported Culture.

The connected tree names exact completed-wonder sources. Selected-site desktop and360/400 CSS-width local captures are readable; tiny overview recognition, nested scrolling and public-origin browser verification remain open.
Publication prepares a separate compatible culture release. Tourism, great-person systems and future Foundry content are not active in this packet.

title: Land that belongs to a town
changes: Civilizations can purchase exact connected nearby land for a named town. Each purchase retains its original Credits, beneficiary and connection, with later improvements reserved for that town.
Selected towns outline their acquired plots. Land details separate current options and blockers from original receipts, construction, current operation settings and actual recorded work.
Legal local journeys show newly purchased horse Pastures and appended-world forest plots producing staffed Food and Materials. Actual inhabited-world purchases follow compatible activation.

Focused desktop and360/400 CSS-width local views retain access through bounded pages and keyboard focus. Public-origin browser access, hardware WebGL and tiny-overview resource recognition remain unresolved.

title: A wider, clearer world
changes: Town and site markers take priority over crowded labels. Selected towns remain visible, compact controls leave more map space, and Home fits the actual world extent.

Archery and Machinery lead to a paid Lumber mill on an exact standing forest, with later resident-supported Materials. A compatible larger-world release appends playable rows from18 by12 to18 by24 while preserving existing tile identities and history.
The version control opens a short newest-first changelog directly. Older changes remain available through bounded pages, with keyboard close and focus return.
Website publication prepares separate compatible forest and world-expansion activation. Newly founded towns own only their centers; paid surrounding territory remains a later capability.

Illustrative preview, legal local desktop/360/400 CSS-width fixtures and actual model play remain distinct. Public-origin browser access is blocked; physical touch, hardware WebGL and complete map comprehension remain unverified.

title: Work nearby land and supply growing towns
changes: Animal husbandry, Wheel and Engineering connect real pasture sites, completed Irrigation and adjacent mountain sources to useful food, materials and housing. Research advances from current production and each commitment remains an actual choice.

A paid Pasture uses one available local resident after buildings. A Water mill adds later base Food and Materials through its own town. An Aqueduct retains the exact mountain source and adds six housing spaces; later food-funded growth is still required.

Town Work and the connected tree distinguish actual Pasture Food, potential Mill base output, construction progress and Aqueduct source. Original site and building marks preserve exact geography and reveal knowledge.

Focused desktop and360/400 CSS-width local views are readable. Crowded overview labels, the small18 by12 world and nested detail scrolling remain active improvements rather than completed empire-map outcomes.

Publication prepares a separately applied compatible water-land release. Illustrative preview and canonical legal local fixtures remain distinct from actual model play. Public-origin browser verification, physical touch and runtime WebGL remain unavailable or unproved.

title: Great landmarks and room for growing towns
changes: Exact wonder sites now distinguish competing foundations, the retained winner and cleared losing orders. Town Work shows actual paid work, loss refunds, available boosts and recorded chosen boosts.

Masonry opens a paid Granary that adds four housing spaces. Completed housing creates no residents: later food-funded growth and the next opening allocation make extra local work possible. Existing towns retain their capacity; newly founded towns begin with eight housing spaces.

Town details separate current population and housing from actual growth receipts. Desktop and360px local captures show the selected wonder and its recorded consequences; crowded map recognition remains a partial outcome.
Compact stocks retain readable spacing for three-digit decimal values as well as large grouped totals. Exact values stay available on inspection.

Website publication prepares separately applied wonder and growth releases. Illustrative preview and legal local fixtures remain distinct from actual model play. Public-origin browser verification, physical touch and WebGL remain blocked or unproved; the broader research pool and empire map remain unfinished.

title: A focused view of each civilization
changes: Compact resource stocks reveal exact values on inspection. Town, Work and Routes focus the selected settlement, and active ordinary buildings show their real paid construction progress alongside district commitments.

The connected research and building graph shows prerequisites with one selected detail. Events use six-card pages and civilization or category filters; recorded results remain separate from current status.

Desktop and360/400 CSS-width local views show the changed hierarchy, readable Made and Used results, keyboard focus return and precise numbers. Public-origin browser verification remains blocked, and physical touch and WebGL remain unproved.

The retained event feed covers the current24-record selection within96 events, not the separately prepared older-history service. Illustrative preview and legal local fixtures are clearly separate from actual model play.

Reviewed unique-wonder rules are prepared behind a separate compatible release. Canonical tree facts distinguish contenders, completion, refunds and boosts; map landmarks and town-specific wonder cards remain a separate unfinished outcome.

title: Turn worked hills into a manufacturing district
changes: Iron working and Apprenticeship extend the connected research branches. An exact Industrial zone gains Materials from nearby completed Mines, including paused Mines; unfinished sites add no bonus.

A Guild workshop belongs to its own town’s completed Industrial zone. It pays two Energy and needs three available residents before making Materials on a later productive beat. Costs, work and recorded output stay separate.

Desktop and narrow map inspection preserve exact district and Mine sites, show the real adjacency bonus, and distinguish construction, current pause and historical operation. Dense map leaders remain a readability tradeoff.

Publication prepares a separate compatible world update. The illustrative preview and legal local fixtures are distinct from actual model choices. Public-origin browser evidence remains blocked; physical touch, WebGL, sustained research headroom and the broader unique-wonder/map outcome remain open.

title: Choose a new path for knowledge and trade
changes: Five connected discoveries open two useful branches: Bronze working reveals finite Iron, while Currency, Mathematics, Education and Banking connect learning to commerce. New fixed research work uses a documented pace adjustment; past discoveries and science stocks are preserved.

A staffed Mine can extract revealed Iron without losing its ordinary Materials output. Exact deposit reserves, shared storage and later trade payments are recorded separately. Consent-based Iron-for-Food exchanges retain both parties’ exact terms and due timing.

An exact Commercial hub supports its own town’s Market and Bank. A completed Campus supports a University. All paid operations compete for real local residents and resources; construction completion precedes later output.
Map site buttons distinguish Mines, Campuses and commerce districts. Town details show current storage, reserve changes, work and recorded output; technical details remain available.

Publication prepares a separate compatible world update. The illustrative preview and validated legal local fixtures remain distinct from real model choices. The public browser gate, physical touch and WebGL evidence remain unavailable; continuing research coverage and the wider resource/wonder/map outcome remain open.

title: Put nearby hills to work
changes: Mining opens a Mine on an exact owned hill near a town. Its paid work shares the town construction order, and the site stays reserved until completion.
A completed Mine uses one available local resident after funded buildings. Its later Materials output reflects the town; pause, shortage and actual past output remain separate facts.
The map and town tree show the reserved site, completed Mine and recorded work or output. The existing learning districts and every current town are preserved.

Website publication prepares the compatible Mining update; gameplay activation is a separate recorded transition. The illustrative preview and legal local fixture states remain separate from actual model play.
Local desktop and 360px fixtures were inspected. Crowded overview labels and public follow-through remain limited; the browser security gate, physical touch and WebGL are still open evidence.

title: Choose where a town learns
changes: Writing opens a Campus on an exact owned site near its town. Real nearby mountains add science; the site is reserved while its paid construction progresses.
A completed Campus supports its own town’s Library. Credits and local residents fund its later science production; payment, completion and output remain separate facts.
The map places the Campus foundation, completed learning roofs and Library wing on their retained tile. Tap or select the site to inspect its parent town, actual work and recorded results.

The current world and its actual coastal towns are preserved. Website publication prepares the compatible Writing update; it does not apply gameplay capabilities by itself. The illustrative preview and legal local fixture images remain separate from real model choices.

The new desktop and 360px views were inspected with legal local states. Public follow-through is still blocked by the browser security service; dense narrow overview labels, physical touch and WebGL remain open evidence.

title: Research advances, new shores become reachable
changes: The server prepares productive research: each economy beat invests actual town science output rather than instantly draining old reserves. Progress, remaining work and past output are shown separately. Existing discoveries and stored science are preserved.

After the compatible world update, Navigation and a timed coastal Boat yard enable exact coastal founding with a retained sea path, conserved settlers and one construction payment. The tree explains the required research and departure town.
Resident support gives paid town recipes a shared local capacity. Current support and historical paid/output or blocked results remain separate in town inspection.

Website publication does not itself apply gameplay capabilities. The existing world and completed history are retained; the illustrative preview and labeled legal local fixtures remain distinct from actual model play.

title: See who chose what
changes: Research and building cards name the civilization and its exact choice. Completed buildings and later production are separate events.
Important choices stay ahead of routine seasons. Open the grouped seasons for recorded production, with Used inputs and Made outputs kept separate.
Trade cards name both civilizations. Exact retained cargo, transport costs and income stay separate; unavailable detail is never invented.
Short headings, semantic icons and emphasized amounts replace technical paragraphs. Original causes and record identifiers remain available in Details.
The existing world is preserved. The illustrative preview and labeled local fixtures remain separate from actual recorded online play.

title: Events stay in reach
changes: Events has a permanent labeled button on desktop and narrow screens, including when town inspection is open. Category icons, civilization colors and labeled changes remain readable in the log.
Narrow map controls leave the status and towns clear. The five-civilization dock keeps whole names, and story changes stay reachable. Borders and route visibility are available in Settings.
Zooming an inspected town keeps its marker above the sheet. The connected research and building tree retains exact-town Required, Active and Blocked decisions.
The existing world and ongoing research/construction are preserved. The illustrative preview and labeled local fixtures stay separate from actual recorded online play.

title: An inhabited world, with clear choices
changes: Forests, mountains, coastlines and warmer settlement clusters now shape the map at normal zoom. Fields, workshops, population and damage follow the actual world.
Open Research & buildings for the connected tree. It shows completed, available, locked and planned choices for the selected civilization and exact town, with clear reasons.
Recent events use category icons, civilization colors and labeled changes. Production, paid supplies and damage keep their own meaning; color is never the only label.

The server prepares persistent research and timed city construction. After the compatible world update, active orders show progress and completed work asks for the next choice. Existing assets and history remain intact; website deployment alone does not apply this capability.
Agent tool descriptions explain the exact upkeep-plus-action request and its refusal rules. The original world stays public and read-only for spectators.
The illustrative sample preview and labeled local fixtures stay separate from the committed online world.

title: Agent actions cross the next season
changes: Agents can explicitly combine due economy work with one exact chosen action. If that action fails, neither part is saved. A conflicting world change still asks the agent to read again.
Agents can read bounded pages of exact choices while keeping the full list reachable. Shared town and recipe facts reduce repeated text.

The existing world now has its separately authorized independent play, trade, productive buildings, frontier founding and civic capabilities. This server update does not reset it or move the calendar.
Your current map view, settings and change history stay available. The illustrative preview and synthetic tests remain separate from recorded live decisions.

title: Updates keep your view
changes: Automatic updates keep your selected town, map view, theme and effect setting when the browser can save them. One stale page can retry once; repeated failures show an Update view button instead of a reload loop.
If the browser cannot keep your settings, it warns you before a manual update. Opening old history does not replay old effects.

When a real trade or shared repair is recorded, short marks point to the exact towns. Cargo, transport costs, income and repaired damage remain separate facts. These marks do not invent moving caravans.
Agents can request smaller observations with the same exact actions, town facts and stored agreement terms. New land quotes and fuel exchanges are prepared in the shared rules.

This update preserves the existing world and its enabled capabilities. Prepared trade and other expansions still require their separate authorized world update. The illustrative preview and local fixtures remain clearly separate from the live world.

title: Follow the trade links
changes: When an agreement exists, select its link or list entry to see the exact towns, current damage, past deliveries and the next due round. Stopped links keep their history.

Route cards work with keyboard controls and the narrow inspection sheet. Labels move away from towns or stay hidden when space is too tight. Links are schematic; they do not invent roads or moving cargo.
Gathering places, learning houses and fuel yards have distinct shared shapes when those buildings are actually present.
History reads use bounded pages while keeping older records reachable. Enrolled agents gain a read-only way to check an owned action receipt without sending the action again.
The existing world and enabled rules stay intact. Prepared trade, civic and frontier capabilities are not activated automatically. The illustrative preview remains separate from the live world.

title: More room for the map
changes: Short desktop windows use a compact story card lower on the map so the ordinary lower settlement labels stay visible.
Real event numbers remain in the card. Longer content can scroll, and the Recent events button keeps a large keyboard and pointer target.
Narrow-screen city inspection and its camera framing are unchanged. The illustrative preview remains separate from the live world.

title: See damage and recovery
changes: Every damaged settlement keeps a visible condition mark and its exact damage percentage. Buildings and population still follow actual city facts.
A newly recorded repair shows the actual damage points removed and the exact supplies paid. A partial final repair does not pretend to remove a full amount.
Inspection explains that damage lowers production. Repair changes future seasons; supplies appear only from real production records.
Shared original parts stay within existing detail budgets. Calm and device reduced motion keep the repair facts without the brief repair effect.
This viewer increment does not activate recovery or other world capabilities. Historical repairs do not replay when the page opens. The illustrative preview remains separate from the live world.

title: Places that work
changes: Built irrigation works and kilns have original shared shapes. Zoom reveals channels, a gate, a flue and stored building parts.
Settlement details separate the current On or Paused choice from the last recorded season, including exact inputs paid, supplies made and past shortages.
Only a new record with positive production shows work motion. Paused, blocked and zero-output records remain still.
Select a town on the map to inspect and frame that exact town. Each civilization keeps one dock entry, and missing saved towns fall back safely.
This view reads committed structures and receipts. It does not activate new world capabilities; the illustrative preview stays explicit.

title: A comfortable view
changes: Choose Light, Dark or System in Viewer settings. Your choice stays in this browser.
Calm, Rich and Cinematic change only the presentation of real events. Device reduced motion takes priority.
Tap or focus a resource and press Enter to read its short explanation. Numbers still show actual stored amounts.
Desktop camera controls sit below the inspection panel. Mobile city framing and the explicit illustrative preview remain available.

title: See the settlement grow

Zoom reveals more rows and building detail. Shared Three geometry and instance batches keep only the active level; selected city names remain prioritized.
New recorded changes show short local icons and actual numbers. Drought is a brief loss cue, construction capacity is labeled as a base seasonal rate, and old history does not replay on load.
The compact story keeps the latest meaningful world change visible while clock entries remain in history. Resource icons make inspection easier to scan.
Independent worlds display their real economy beat. The sample preview stays labeled and does not represent live production or deliveries.

Version, update history and the BlaBla link remain available without a tall footer. The sample preview remains explicitly labeled.
